subject: Renewal: Dedicated capacity expansion — concurrency slots vs hard cap burst
content:
----Email 1 of 6----
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Huang <claire@fintechco.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 16:15:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion — sizing + burst policy options

Hi Claire,

Hope you're doing well — quick note as we approach your June 1 renewal for the Dedicated pool. Per our last usage report you're averaging 350 concurrent tokens/sec with daily peaks up to 900 tokens/sec (short bursts ~10–30s). Rather than a straight commit increase, I wanted to propose two paths for capacity expansion that fit different risk profiles:

1) Incremental Reserved GPUs + concurrency slots (recommended)
   - Add 4x A100 reserved GPUs to the pool
   - Guarantee baseline throughput for 400 tokens/sec, with additional concurrency slots that allow short bursts up to 1,200 tokens/sec
   - Burst policy: on-demand overflow to shared Hosted capacity billed at 1.5x reserved rate, with a monthly cap on overflow spend

2) Hardened cap with purchase buffer
   - Add 6x reserved GPUs but hard cap burst to 600 tokens/sec to avoid any spillover to Hosted
   - Lower per-token variability and simpler billing, but higher committed cost

I attached a short term sheet and an SLA appendix with the throughput and billing examples. Can you share which option you'd prefer, and whether procurement needs a specific legal addendum for the overflow billing model?

Thanks — happy to walk through numbers on a call this week.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192

Attachments: Redwood-Termsheet-FIN-2027-042.pdf (pdf), Redwood-SLA-appendix-FIN-2027-042.pdf (pdf)

----Email 2 of 6----
From: Claire Huang <claire@fintechco.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — sizing + burst policy options

Sean — thanks for the clear options. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we pull procurement in:

- Our main concern is user experience during payroll cutoffs (monthly end) — bursts last ~2–3 minutes and we currently tolerate a 5–7% latency tail. If we move to the overflow model, how do you guarantee we won't exceed our error budget?

- For the concurrency slots approach: are the slots FIFO, or can we prioritize certain routes (transactional endpoints) so critical flows never get queued behind embeddings jobs?

Procurement will want both a sample invoice and any addendum language for "overflow usage." Could you also outline activation lead time if we sign by May 1?

—Claire
Claire Huang
Director of AI Platform | FinTechCo

----Email 3 of 6----
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Huang <claire@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — sizing + burst policy options

Thanks Claire — answering inline:

> how do you guarantee we won't exceed our error budget?

We expose per-route latency SLIs and an overflow guardrail: if queueing-driven p99 latency approaches the configured threshold, traffic is automatically routed to a compatible higher-capacity variant (warm fallback) or to Hosted spillover. We also offer a monthly "overflow credit" threshold: if overflow spend would exceed X% of committed spend, we send a warning and automatically throttle non-critical routes.

> are the concurrency slots FIFO, or can we prioritize certain routes?

Slots are configurable by route. You can pin priority slots to up to 6 named endpoints (transactional routes), and the remainder are for best-effort tasks. We can show a config example.

Activation lead time: 10 business days from fully executed DocuSign (hardware scheduling + provisioning + model onboarding and smoke tests). If you sign by May 1, we can target activation by May 15.

Looping in Marissa and Lauren to put the pricing and the addendum language in the thread.

-Sean

----Email 4 of 6----
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Huang <claire@fintechco.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — sizing + burst policy options

Hi Claire,

Attached is a revised term sheet and a one-page "Overflow Addendum" for procurement. Highlights:

- Option A (recommended): +4 reserved A100s, baseline throughput 400 tokens/sec, 2,000 concurrency slots, burst to 1,200 tokens/sec via Hosted spillover
  - Price delta: +$36,000/mo
  - Overflow billing: 1.5x reserved per-token rate. Monthly overflow credit cap = $5,000. Overages beyond credit require pre-approval.
  - SLA: 99.9% availability for baseline capacity; latency SLOs defined per route in appendix.

- Option B (low variability): +6 reserved A100s, baseline throughput 600 tokens/sec, hard cap on burst (no spillover)
  - Price delta: +$55,000/mo
  - SLA: 99.95% availability for committed capacity

Procurement language included: sample invoice, PO instructions, and a short legal addendum clause that defines "overflow usage" and the pre-approval flow.

Attachments: Redwood-Termsheet-FIN-2027-042-rev1.pdf, Overflow-Addendum-FIN-2027-042.pdf

Happy to jump on a 30m call to run through numbers.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Sales Director | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Team — procurement here. A few points:

1) We need the overflow addendum redlineable as a standalone exhibit. Please provide in Word (we prefer docx).
2) Confirmation that overflow billing will be consolidated on the monthly invoice with a clear line item and that we can receive daily usage exports for the first 90 days.
3) For Option A, what are the termination rights if overflow spend routinely hits the cap? We want an SLA credit + a termination window.

Also, Claire requested a firm activation date in case we need to schedule change freezes.

Thanks,
David Li

procure@fintechco.com

Hi David/Claire — thanks for the clarity. We've uploaded the Overflow Addendum in both PDF and DOCX and attached the revised term sheet. Quick answers:

- We'll deliver the docx redline by EOD Thu, Apr 15. Link: https://drive.google.com/fintechco/renewal-2027
- Overflow billing will appear as "Hosted Spillover (tokens)" on the monthly invoice; daily usage CSVs available via S3 dump for the first 90 days.
- Termination: For Option A we propose a quarterly review window. If monthly overflow spend > 20% of committed monthly fee for 2 consecutive months, customer may elect 30-day termination with prorated refunds for pre-paid months and SLA credits. Language included in addendum.
- Firm activation: sign by May 1 → target activation May 15. We can support a 48-hour ramp to full capacity if change freeze schedules are locked.

Next steps: we will send DocuSign for FIN-2027-042 (Option A) and the docx addendum. Once executed, our provisioning team will confirm exact activation date and share the runbook.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Account Manager | Redwood Inference
